meta.title: Baking Is a Compile Step
meta.subtitle: A source language, a dependency-tracked front end, whole-program passes, a strip, and an object file you ship

views.label: The front end
views.note: One baker per authoring component, and every read it makes is recorded as the key that decides whether it re-runs.

views.label: The whole-scene passes
views.note: Bakers cannot see each other. The systems that run after them can see everything at once.

views.label: The object file
views.note: What ships is a serialized chunk image, one file per section, with no authoring objects left in it.

views.label: Nothing bakes at runtime
views.note: The player contains no bakers. If a value is wrong at runtime, it was already wrong before the build.

nodes.label: GameObject
nodes.sublabel: components you can see and drag

nodes.label: Entity section file

cards.title: The passes, in the order they run
items: Pre-baking group, for cleanup before anything is read · Baking/BakingUtility.cs:142
Every baker, one per authoring component, in a transient world · :200
Transform baking, then the ordinary baking systems · :151, :157
Post-baking, then the strip pass that deletes the scaffolding · :181, :187

cards.title: Why a baker cannot look around
items: A baker only sees the component it was given, plus anything it explicitly asks for
Every such ask is recorded, and that record is what decides whether it re-runs
Read something without declaring it and your edit silently changes nothing
Anything that needs the whole scene belongs in a baking system, not a baker

cards.title: The strip pass is the linker's dead-code pass
items: Every type marked temporary is queried and removed before serialization · Baking/BakingStripSystem.cs:42
So scaffolding components exist during the bake and never reach the player
The baking groups are all marked disable-auto-creation; they exist only in the baking world
Which is why nothing on this map can be inspected at runtime

cards.title: Sections are the output units
items: A shared component partitions the baked entities into numbered sections
Each section is moved into a private world and serialized on its own
Section zero is the one that always loads; the rest are separately requestable
That partition is decided at bake time, so streaming granularity is a compile-time choice
